name: Vladimir Bukovsky
milestone_by_age_26: First arrested in 1963 at age 20-21 for possessing forbidden literature and organizing dissident activities; Soviet authorities declared him mentally ill and confined him to a psychiatric hospital, making him a prominent figure in the Soviet dissident movement by his early twenties.
early_history_summary: Born in Belebey, Bashkir ASSR during WWII evacuation, Bukovsky returned to Moscow with his family after the war. His father was a well-known Soviet journalist. He was expelled from school for creating an unauthorized magazine, then entered Moscow State University in 1960 to study biology but was expelled at 19 for criticizing Soviet state organizations. He helped revive the Mayakovsky Square poetry readings. In 1963, he was first arrested and sent to a psychiatric hospital — the beginning of 12 years of imprisonment that defined his dissident career.
family_context_summary: Born to Russian parents; father Konstantin (1908-1976) was a well-known Soviet journalist. Family was evacuated to Bashkir ASSR during WWII, then returned to Moscow. The family had intellectual and media connections through the father's journalism career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a well-known Soviet journalist, providing exposure to media, communications, and intellectual circles in Moscow, though there is no evidence this directly facilitated Bukovsky's dissident activities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father was Soviet journalist,Moscow University access,dissident peer network,Soviet repression as catalyst,Mayakovsky Square readings
evidence_summary: Vladimir Bukovsky became a prominent Soviet dissident by his early twenties, with his first arrest in 1963 at age 20-21 for possessing forbidden literature and subsequent forced psychiatric hospitalization. His father was a well-known Soviet journalist, providing intellectual and media environment exposure. He was expelled from Moscow State University at 19 for criticizing Soviet organizations, and helped organize the Mayakovsky Square poetry readings. The adversity of Soviet repression served as a powerful catalyst for his activism, and his peer network of dissidents (Yuri Galanskov, Vladimir Osipov) provided collaborative support. His milestone of arrest and psychiatric hospitalization was independently verified by multiple sources.
starting_point: Born to a well-known Soviet journalist father and Russian mother in Belebey, Bashkir ASSR (wartime evacuation); family returned to Moscow after WWII. Intellectual family background.
current_position: Died on October 27, 2019, at age 76 in Cambridge, England, of cardiac arrest. Final role: writer and human rights activist based in Cambridge.

early_history_summary: Born in Saint-Pierre, Réunion, Richardson started playing handball at age 6 when he followed his older brother to training. He spent his entire youth career at Saint-Pierre HBC (1977-1989). In 1988, at age 19, he was spotted by French national team coach Daniel Costantini during a match on Réunion Island and brought to mainland France via the Bataillon de Joinville military sport program. He signed for Paris-Asnières in 1989 and debuted for France in 1990, immediately being voted MVP of the World Championship.

name: Alex Trebek
milestone_by_age_26: Hosted Music Hop (1963-64), CBC Television's first live teen music show, at age 23-24, establishing himself as a national broadcaster on Canada's premier television network.
early_history_summary: Born in Sudbury, Ontario to a Ukrainian immigrant father (a hotel chef) and Franco-Ontarian mother, Trebek grew up bilingual in French and English. He attended the University of Ottawa, graduating with a philosophy degree in 1961. While still a student, he began working at CBC Radio in Ottawa, and upon graduation became a full-time staff announcer. He transferred to Toronto and was given hosting duties for Music Hop (1963-64), CBC's first live teen music show, at age 23.
family_context_summary: Son of a Ukrainian immigrant father (George Edward Trebek, born Terebeychuk) who worked as a hotel chef, and a Franco-Ontarian mother (Lucille Marie Lagacé). Grew up in a bilingual French-English household in Sudbury, Ontario. Working-class background; his first job at 13 was as a bellhop at the hotel where his father worked.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of parental involvement in broadcasting or media. Father was a chef, not connected to the broadcasting industry.

evidence_summary: Alex Trebek leveraged the CBC's national broadcasting platform to become a TV host by age 23, hosting Music Hop (1963-64), Canada's first live teen music show. He came from a working-class background — his father was a Ukrainian immigrant chef — and gained entry to broadcasting through a summer job at CBC Radio while studying at the University of Ottawa. His bilingual French-English ability was an asset at CBC. No family wealth or media connections were documented; his advantage was the CBC institutional pipeline and direct early domain exposure in broadcasting.
